content.title: Parametric Derivatives: Finding dy/dx
content.overview: In AP Calculus BC, parametric equations define x and y as functions of a third variable, usually time (t). This lesson focuses on calculating the first derivative, dy/dx, which represents the slope of the tangent line to the curve in the xy-plane, by relating the rates of change of x and y with respect to the parameter t.
learning_objectives: Define the first derivative of a parametric curve in terms of the parameter t.
Calculate the slope of a tangent line to a parametric curve at a specific value of t.
Identify conditions under which the parametric derivative is undefined or zero.
Apply the parametric derivative formula to analytical, tabular, and contextual data.

sections.title: The Parametric Derivative Formula
sections.content:
For a curve defined by the parametric equations x = f(t) and y = g(t), the derivative dy/dx represents the instantaneous rate of change of y with respect to x. According to the Chain Rule, dy/dt = (dy/dx) * (dx/dt). By rearranging this relationship, we find that dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt), provided that dx/dt is not equal to zero. This allows us to find the slope of the tangent line in the xy-plane without needing to eliminate the parameter t to find a direct function y = f(x).

![A linear sequence showing the steps to find dy/dx: Differentiate x(t), Differentiate y(t), Divide dy/dt by dx/dt, Evaluate at the given t.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/7879b64e-e0cd-48c4-8865-31275f6e7c23-1786526330377-236.webp)

sections.title: Horizontal and Vertical Tangents
sections.content: The behavior of the parametric derivative dy/dx reveals the orientation of the tangent line. A horizontal tangent occurs when the slope dy/dx is zero, which happens when dy/dt = 0 and dx/dt is non-zero. A vertical tangent occurs when the slope is undefined, which happens when dx/dt = 0 and dy/dt is non-zero. If both derivatives are zero simultaneously, the limit of the ratio must be evaluated, often using L'Hôpital's Rule, to determine the behavior of the curve.

sections.title: Interpreting Tabular and Analytical Data
sections.content: On the AP Exam, you may be asked to determine dy/dx using a table of values for x'(t) and y'(t) or by differentiating given functions f(t) and g(t). When given a specific point (x, y), you must first identify the corresponding value of t before applying the derivative formula. Always ensure that the units of dy/dx are the units of y divided by the units of x, regardless of the units of the parameter t.

worked_examples.question: A particle moves along a curve defined by x(t) = t^2 + 3t and y(t) = sin(πt). Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve at t = 1.
worked_examples.solution:
Step 1: Find dx/dt. Differentiating x(t) with respect to t gives dx/dt = 2t + 3.
Step 2: Find dy/dt. Differentiating y(t) with respect to t using the chain rule gives dy/dt = π * cos(πt).
Step 3: Evaluate both derivatives at t = 1. 
dx/dt | t=1 = 2(1) + 3 = 5. 
dy/dt | t=1 = π * cos(π) = π * (-1) = -π.
Step 4: Apply the parametric derivative formula: dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt). 
dy/dx = -π / 5. The slope of the tangent line at t = 1 is -π/5.

common_mistakes: Inverting the formula and calculating dx/dy (dx/dt divided by dy/dt) instead of dy/dx.
Forgetting to use the Chain Rule when differentiating x(t) or y(t) with respect to t.
Assuming dy/dx is simply y'(t) without dividing by x'(t).
Failing to check if dx/dt = 0, which would make the derivative undefined.
exam_tips: Always show the setup (dy/dt) / (dx/dt) before plugging in numbers to earn partial credit on FRQs.
If a question asks for the slope at a point (a, b), solve for t first by setting x(t) = a and y(t) = b.
Remember that dy/dx is a function of t, not x, unless you explicitly eliminate the parameter.
content.recap: The derivative dy/dx for a parametric curve is the ratio of the vertical rate of change (dy/dt) to the horizontal rate of change (dx/dt). This value represents the slope of the tangent line in the xy-plane and is essential for analyzing the motion and geometry of curves defined parametrically.

knowledge_claims.content: The first derivative of a parametric curve, dy/dx, is calculated as (dy/dt) / (dx/dt).
The parametric derivative dy/dx is only defined when the horizontal rate of change, dx/dt, is not equal to zero.
The value of dy/dx represents the slope of the tangent line to the curve in the xy-plane at a specific value of the parameter t.
A horizontal tangent to a parametric curve occurs at values of t where dy/dt = 0 and dx/dt is non-zero.
A vertical tangent to a parametric curve occurs at values of t where dx/dt = 0 and dy/dt is non-zero.
To find the slope of a parametric curve at a given point (x, y), one must first determine the value of the parameter t that corresponds to that coordinate.
It is a common error to calculate the derivative as dy/dt instead of the ratio (dy/dt)/(dx/dt).
If dy/dt and dx/dt are both zero at a point, L'Hôpital's Rule may be required to find the limit of the slope as t approaches that value.
The units of the parametric derivative dy/dx are (units of y) / (units of x), independent of the units of t.
In the context of particle motion, dy/dx represents the ratio of the vertical component of velocity to the horizontal component of velocity.
When evaluating dy/dx from a table, ensure you are selecting the values for the derivatives x'(t) and y'(t) rather than the position values x(t) and y(t).
The Chain Rule provides the underlying mathematical justification for the parametric derivative formula: dy/dt = (dy/dx) * (dx/dt).

items.stem: Which procedure or value is mathematically consistent in “AP Calculus BC — Parametric Derivatives — Practice Record 01”?

options.A: Parametric Derivatives: For a parametric curve, dy/dx is the quotient of derivatives with respect to the parameter when dx/dt is nonzero.
options.B: Geometric and Telescoping Series: A geometric series converges for common-ratio magnitude below one, while telescoping series simplify through cancellation of partial sums.
options.C: Limits from Tables and Graphs: A limit describes the value approached by a function and can be estimated from values or graph behavior on both sides of the input.
options.D: Higher-Order Derivatives: Successive derivatives describe changing rates, such as velocity from position and acceleration from velocity, with units changing at each differentiation.

items.explanation: Choice A is best because For a parametric curve, dy/dx is the quotient of derivatives with respect to the parameter when dx/dt is nonzero. The other options invoke different atomic topics and do not satisfy the record's stated target as directly.

items.stem: Which relationship connects the verbal and symbolic information in “AP Calculus BC — Parametric Derivatives — Practice Record 02”?

options.A: Integral and p-Series Tests: Positive decreasing terms may be compared with an improper integral, and a p-series converges exactly when its exponent exceeds one.
options.B: Parametric Derivatives: For a parametric curve, dy/dx is the quotient of derivatives with respect to the parameter when dx/dt is nonzero.
options.C: Algebraic Evaluation of Limits: Direct substitution works when expressions are continuous; indeterminate forms may require factoring, rationalizing, or equivalent algebraic restructuring.
options.D: Chain Rule: The derivative of a composite function multiplies the derivative of the outer function evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

items.explanation: Choice B is best because For a parametric curve, dy/dx is the quotient of derivatives with respect to the parameter when dx/dt is nonzero. The other options invoke different atomic topics and do not satisfy the record's stated target as directly.
